environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: The upstream sends `Content-Length: 5` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with a 15-byte chunk stream. The proxy relays the chunk framing verbatim but sizes its own emitted body from the Content-Length, so only the first 5 bytes of the chunk stream reach the client. A client that honours Transfer-Encoding reads a chunk size of 5 and then receives `HE` with no CRLF and no terminating zero chunk; the payload tail and the terminator never arrive. Silent under Connection: close, five of five cold replicates byte-identical with passing controls.
findings.title: A relayed response with both Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Length is cut at the Content-Length while still chunk-framed

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line

author_attested: analysis metadata reconstructed after the run
verified: release tag resolves to the submitted source
source SHA-256 and report and evidence hashes

scope: Upstream that emits both framing headers with a chunk stream longer than its Content-Length; client-side framing, upstream-driven
